title: Sigil and Salt Anew
premise: Yara Villalobos has spent their whole life in the Salt Valley, the one place in Vessia where magic cannot follow, hiding among exiles who traded their gifts for safety. When King Aldric's crown announces a purge of all gifted people, Yara learns the truth: the king died years ago, and a hollow thing wearing his crown now feeds on dragon-fire to sustain its stolen reign. Fleeing the valley for the first time, Yara must reclaim their storm-calling, gather a found family of hunted magicians, and unbind the dead king from the usurper before the last dragon's flame gutters out and magic dies with it. In the end, Yara chooses neither crown nor exile but a third path—dissolving the monarchy's claim over magic itself—and finds belonging not in a place that accepts them, but in people who know them fully.
about_author: Mirabel Thornbury is the pen name of a former cartographer who once mapped coastlines for a living and now maps impossible ones instead. They write fantasy about outsiders, weather, and the families we build when our birthplaces refuse us.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. We meet the Salt Valley, where magic cannot cross the salt flats, and Yara's quiet life mending nets and hiding their storm-scarred hands. A new exile arrives with news of the crown's hunt. Emotional beat: the fragile comfort of invisibility beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Salt on the Tongue
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The valley elders vote to bar the newcomer, Odessa, whose gift of reading fire makes her a beacon for the hunters. Yara argues for sheltering her—the first time they've spoken up in years. Emotional beat: guilt over a lifetime of silence hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Crown Announced
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. She recounts the royal proclamation: every gifted person to be registered, then 'bound.' She reveals she saw the king at court and something was wrong with him—his shadow moved against the light. Emotional beat: dread arriving ahead of the hunters themselves.

chapters.title: Riders on the Flats
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Crown wardens breach the salt line using an artifact that lets them carry binding-iron across it. The valley's protection is broken. In the chaos, Yara's suppressed gift sparks involuntarily, lightning splitting the sky. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration tangled together.

chapters.title: The First Storm in Twenty Years
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara's outburst saves the valley but marks them; the wardens retreat with Yara's name. The elders demand they leave. Odessa offers to guide them toward the capital and the truth about the king. Emotional beat: exile from the place of exile—grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Crossing Over
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara steps past the salt line for the first time and their magic floods back, overwhelming and unfamiliar. Odessa teaches them to hold it like breath rather than weapon. Emotional beat: identity returning like a lost limb waking—painful, alive.

chapters.title: The Ember Road
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. On the road to the capital, they find a burned waystation and a survivor: Bramble, a child hedge-witch who hid in a root cellar while her family was bound. Emotional beat: the hunt's cost made flesh; Yara's protective instinct ignites.

chapters.title: A Tavern of Small Magics
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They shelter at the Gilded Wren, an inn secretly run by gifted folk—a node of resistance led by Perrin, a former royal binder who deserted. He confirms Odessa's story: the king is dead, and something else rules. Emotional beat: cautious hope; the first taste of community outside the valley.

chapters.title: Perrin's Confession
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. Perrin reveals he helped create the binding-iron and the ritual that let the usurper take the throne—he believed he was saving the kingdom from magical civil war. Emotional beat: shame as a form of penance; trust extended grudgingly and earned slowly.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Disguised as warden conscripts, they infiltrate the capital and witness the 'king'—a crowned absence, sustained by siphoned dragon-fire, feeding on the bound gifts of captured magicians. Emotional beat: horror transmuted into clarity about what must be undone.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. Beneath the palace burns the last dragon, Vaskarath, chained as the usurper's living furnace. Odessa can hear her dying thoughts through the fire. Emotional beat: grief for a dying ancient being; the stakes become mortal and mythic at once.

chapters.title: Bramble Stolen
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Their cover breaks; Bramble is seized by wardens to be bound and fed to the crown. Yara's storm rises unbidden, half-destroying a city block. Emotional beat: rage without control—the danger of becoming what they fight.

chapters.title: Learning to Hold Lightning
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. Hiding in the undercity, Perrin trains Yara using the very binding techniques he invented—not to cage their power but to give it shape. Emotional beat: mentorship as atonement; Yara learning that discipline is not suppression.

chapters.title: The Resistance of Small Gifts
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Gilded Wren network mobilizes: hedge-witches, weather-readers, ember-speakers, each small gift essential. They plan to sever the crown's siphon during the Binding Day ceremony. Emotional beat: belonging forged in shared risk—found family crystallizing.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Wren
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. A desperate refugee sells them out; wardens raid the inn. Perrin stays behind to hold the door and is captured. The survivors scatter into the sewers. Emotional beat: loss and fury; the cost of trusting a broken world.

chapters.title: What the Usurper Wants
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Captured briefly and brought before the crown-thing, Yara learns its nature: a hunger older than the kingdom, wearing Aldric because a crown is the easiest shape to rule through. It offers Yara a place beside it. Emotional beat: temptation met and refused—identity claimed outright.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Spire
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Rescued by Odessa and Bramble, Yara calls a true storm for the first time—shaped, deliberate, theirs—to shatter the warden garrison. Emotional beat: triumph laced with fear of their own capacity; power accepted as self, not other.

chapters.title: Binding Day
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. During the public ceremony where hundreds will be bound, the resistance strikes: Odessa frees Vaskarath's chain, Perrin—escaping captivity—reverses his own binding-iron, and Yara walks into the heart of the crowd. Emotional beat: terror and solidarity at maximum pitch.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Climax. Yara channels the freed dragon-fire and their own storm into the crown, unbinding every captive gift at once and burning the hunger out of the coronet. The dead king's shade, released, bows to Yara before dissolving. Emotional beat: catharsis—the storm finally at peace with its own name.

chapters.title: Ashes and Offerings
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. Aftermath: Vaskarath, freed, chooses to remain and share her fire so magic need never be caged again. The council of regents falters; the people look to Yara, who refuses any crown. Emotional beat: exhaustion, mourning for Perrin's wounds and the fallen, tentative dawn.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Without a Crown Over Magic
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Months later, a new accord: magic answers no throne. Yara helps build the Concord, a circle of gifted and ungifted stewards. Bramble begins training; Perrin rebuilds what he broke. Emotional beat: justice outside the law taking institutional root without losing its soul.

chapters.title: Where the Salt Meets the Rain
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara returns to the Salt Valley—not to hide, but to show the elders the person they exiled, and to invite the valley into the wider world. Standing between salt and storm, Yara finally belongs everywhere and needs nowhere to prove it. Emotional beat: homecoming redefined; identity complete.
